hook.line: A good reporter separates what she knows from what she was told. Spanish lets her do that with one small change in the verb, so the paper passes the claim on without promising it is true.
hook.es: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos.
hook.en: According to the paper, the company allegedly paid bribes.

examples.es: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos.
examples.en: According to the paper, the company allegedly paid bribes.

examples.es: El acusado estaría fuera del país.
Según un vecino, Altamira ya habría comprado tres edificios.
examples.en: According to a neighbour, Altamira has reportedly already bought three buildings.

examples.es: Según la radio, el presidente viajaría mañana a Cartagena.
examples.en: According to the radio, the president is reportedly travelling to Cartagena tomorrow.

examples.es: Según una vecina, el dueño vendería el edificio.
examples.en: According to a neighbour, the owner is reportedly going to sell the building.

rule:
Say *La empresa pagó sobornos* and you stand behind it. Put the verb in the conditional and you only pass it on: "that is what I am told".

For now or later, use the simple conditional: *estaría*, *tendría*, *vendería*.
For the past, use the conditional perfect: *habría pagado*, *habría comprado*.

There is no "if" and no "would" here. English adds words like "allegedly" or "reportedly", while Spanish changes the verb. It lives in news and formal reports, and a *según...* often names the source.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the conditional of rumour, or *condicional de rumor*, and in journalism it is a way of reporting without taking responsibility for the claim.

readAndPick.es: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos.
options: The company allegedly paid bribes.
The company paid bribes, and the paper is sure.
Nobody paid bribes.

readAndPick.es: El acusado estaría fuera del país.
options: The accused is definitely abroad.
The accused is reportedly abroad.
The accused would like to leave the country.
The mayor reportedly signed the contract.
The mayor might sign the contract.
The mayor signed the contract (stated as fact).

readAndPick.es: Según un vecino, Altamira ya habría comprado tres edificios.
options: Altamira will buy three buildings.
A neighbour is sure that Altamira bought three buildings.
A neighbour says that Altamira has reportedly already bought three buildings.

readAndPick.es: Según la radio, el presidente viajaría mañana a Cartagena.
options: The president will definitely travel to Cartagena.
The president is reportedly travelling to Cartagena tomorrow.
The president travelled to Cartagena yesterday.
The police reportedly have evidence.
The police had evidence.
The police need evidence.

readAndPick.es: Según una vecina, el dueño vendería el edificio.
options: The owner has sold the building.
The owner wants to buy the building.
The owner is reportedly going to sell the building.

readAndPick.es: Hernando habría salido antes de las ocho.
options: Hernando will leave before eight.
Hernando reportedly left before eight.
Hernando leaves before eight every day.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Según el diario, la empresa ___ sobornos.* (*pagó* or *habría pagado*) According to the paper, the company allegedly paid bribes.
yourTurn.answer: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos.
yourTurn.why: For a claim about the past that you only pass on, use the conditional perfect: *habría pagado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *El acusado ___ fuera del país.* (*está* or *estaría*) The accused is reportedly abroad.
yourTurn.answer: El acusado estaría fuera del país.
yourTurn.why: For a claim about now, the simple conditional *estaría* keeps your distance.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: According to a neighbour, Altamira has reportedly already bought three buildings.
yourTurn.answer: Según un vecino, Altamira ya habría comprado tres edificios.
accept: Según un vecino, Altamira habría comprado ya tres edificios.
yourTurn.why: *Habría comprado* reports the purchase without vouching for it.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: According to the radio, the president is reportedly travelling to Cartagena tomorrow.
yourTurn.answer: Según la radio, el presidente viajaría mañana a Cartagena.
accept: Según la radio, el presidente viajaría a Cartagena mañana.
El presidente viajaría mañana a Cartagena, según la radio.
yourTurn.why: *Viajaría* turns a plan into a reported plan.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The police reportedly have evidence.
accept: Según fuentes cercanas, la policía tendría pruebas.
yourTurn.why: *Tendría* is the conditional of *tener*, and it does not promise that the evidence exists.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *El alcalde habría firmado el contrato.* (The mayor reportedly did not sign the contract.)
yourTurn.answer: El alcalde no habría firmado el contrato.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes in front of *habría*, just like with any other verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn this fact into a rumour: *Hernando salió antes de las ocho.*
yourTurn.answer: Hernando habría salido antes de las ocho.
yourTurn.why: The conditional perfect turns a plain past into a reported past.

pitfalls.wrong: Según el diario, la empresa habrá pagado sobornos.
pitfalls.right: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Habrá pagado* is you guessing, while *habría pagado* passes on what the source says.

pitfalls.wrong: Según el diario, la empresa pagaría sobornos el año pasado.
pitfalls.right: Según el diario, la empresa habría pagado sobornos el año pasado.
pitfalls.why: For something that already happened, you need the conditional perfect.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo vi que el alcalde habría firmado el contrato.
pitfalls.right: Yo vi que el alcalde firmó el contrato.
pitfalls.why: If you saw it yourself, you vouch for it, so use the plain past.

personal: Write two harmless bits of gossip you have heard about a neighbour or a famous person. Start each one with *según...* and put the verb in the conditional.
